Unit 10 • HL

The HL Case Study

Introduction

Can you solve a problem that doesn't exist yet?

This unit prepares you for Paper 1, Section B (HL Extension). Unlike SL, you must dive deeper into the technical challenges (e.g., vSLAM, Neural Processing) and provide Strategic Justifications for your solutions. It's not just about knowing the technology; it's about evaluating its feasibility in a complex, real-world scenario.

You'll start by researching the HL Extension Topics (specific to the current Case Study). Then you'll synthesize this research with your Core CS knowledge to build comprehensive, justified strategies for the client.

Deep Research (HL)

Surface level isn't enough. You need expert evidence.

  • Academic Literacy: Reading white papers and journals.
  • Evidence Bank: Building a library of real-world deployments (e.g., "How NASA uses vSLAM").

Strategic Justification

Why is your solution the BEST one? (Evaluation).

  • Trade-offs: Acknowledgement that every choice has a cost (Latency vs Accuracy).
  • Operational Constraints: Does it work in the rain? Does the battery last?

Technical Synthesis

Connecting the dots.

  • Cross-Topic Logic: Linking Case Study challenges to Coursework concepts (e.g., "This Rescue Robot needs A* Pathfinding (Topic 5) and Sensors (Topic 7)").

The 12-Mark Essay

Structuring a high-level argument.

  • Balanced Account: Arguing FOR and AGAINST your own solution.
  • Conclusion: A final, decisive judgment backed by evidence.

Key Terminology
TermDefinition
SynthesisThe combination of ideas to form a theory or system (Linking Case Study to Syllabus).
Strategic JustificationProviding valid reasons or evidence to support a chosen course of action.
Operational ConstraintsLimitations imposed by the real-world environment (e.g., Battery life, Bandwidth, Weight).
Peer-reviewed ResearchArticles written by experts and reviewed by other experts in the field (Gold standard evidence).
ScalabilityThe capability of a system to handle a growing amount of work.
FeasibilityThe state or degree of being easily or conveniently done.

Common Misconceptions

More Jargon is Better

Don't just list buzzwords. Explain HOW the technology solves the SPECIFIC problem in the scenario.

Ignore the Drawbacks

A Level 7 answer ALWAYS admits the flaws. Perfect solutions don't exist in the real world.

It's just an English Essay

No. It's a Technical Report disguised as an essay. You need specific details (Algorithms, Protocols, Specs).

Real-World Uses

  • Disaster Response Robots (vSLAM)
  • Autonomous Logistics (Pathfinding)
  • Medical Triage AI (Neural Nets)
  • Smart City Infrastructure (IoT)

Think Deeper

"The Cost of Innovation" New technology is expensive and risky. When is it better to stick with 'Old Reliable' technology rather than upgrading to the cutting edge?
